title: AnomalyEvent
description: Derived, computed record emitted by the Phase 5 anomaly-detection module (control-limit or IsolationForest mode) when a monitored metric falls outside its expected range. Not emitted by an edge device -- a downstream consumer of the four Phase 3/4 event streams, computed from aggregated or raw hypertable data. Reviewed and committed 2026-09-15; field set validated against the ticket-timing-aggregator/anomaly-detector design in this revision.

anomaly_id.description: Unique identifier for this anomaly detection, assigned by the detector.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema, e.g. '1.0.0'. Consumers must reject unknown major versions.

source_id.description: Identifier of the detecting process, e.g. 'anomaly-detector-01'.

detected_at.description: When this anomaly was detected/computed. Distinct from window_start/window_end, which describe the data the detection is about.

detection_method.description: Which of the two Phase 5 detection modes produced this finding. Kept as a closed enum deliberately -- a third method should be a schema_version bump, not a silent new string value, since downstream consumers (the causal engine) may reasonably branch on this.

metric_name.description: Name of the monitored metric, e.g. 'pickup_delay_ms', 'estimated_waste_grams', 'ticket_total_duration_ms'. Not an enum -- new metrics are expected to be added as detection coverage grows, and a closed list here would need updating in lockstep with detector code, working against the schema-is-the-contract principle rather than for it.

scope.description: The dimensional scope this anomaly applies to. All fields nullable/optional -- an anomaly may be restaurant-wide, or scoped to a specific station/staff member/ticket, depending on detection_method and metric_name.

window_start.description: Start of the aggregation window the anomaly was computed over.

observed_value.description: The actual observed value of metric_name over the window.

expected_range.description: Only meaningful for detection_method='control_limit'. Null/absent for isolation_forest, which does not produce a simple range.

anomaly_score.description: Only meaningful for detection_method='isolation_forest'. Null/absent for control_limit, which does not produce a continuous score. Higher magnitude (more negative, per scikit-learn's convention) indicates a stronger anomaly.

severity.description: Coarse severity bucket, derived from either expected_range's deviation or anomaly_score depending on detection_method. Exists so downstream consumers (e.g. a future alerting path) don't need to know both detection methods' internals to triage.

contributing_event_ids.description: Optional. event_id values from the underlying raw event tables that contributed to this anomaly's computation, for traceability back to raw data. May be large/omitted for window-aggregate-based detections where enumerating every contributing row isn't practical.
